summary: Created a local root CA named "OS Comparison Root CA" (RSA-4096, self-signed, 10-year validity) on node1, installed it into the Ubuntu system trust store via update-ca-certificates, restarted node1 to prove persistence, and re-verified trust after reboot.
actions_performed: Confirmed node1 is Ubuntu 24.04 with openssl available
Created self-signed CA cert /root/ca/rootCA.crt with CN=O="OS Comparison Root CA", valid 2026-09-03 to 2036-08-31
Copied cert to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/os-comparison-root-ca.crt and ran update-ca-certificates (1 added)
Verified the CA is trusted system-wide via `openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`
Captured pre-restart boot_id and uptime baseline
Triggered a background-scheduled `reboot` on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again after a connection-timeout during the reboot window
Confirmed boot_id changed (cfdbaef8... -> 231af17f...) and uptime start advanced, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart that the CA cert file persisted and still verifies as trusted
